task: Stable model visibility during Fly / Walk and optional whole-map resource preloading

reference.method: Opened the live reference 3D map and Fly controls, read the modulepreload URL from DOM, and fetched the public client read-only. The relevant functions match .reference/3d-route.js.
observedStrategies: Nearby tile loading with a wider retention boundary

causes: Navigation syncTarget uses a 12-game-metre look target; using Orbit target distance accidentally restricted buildings/trees/props to 420/180/90m in balanced mode.
Strict frustum selection plus delayed selection/loading causes newly revealed geometry to pop in when turning.
Finer LOD triangles can exhaust the budget and displace other coarse outlines.
Switching to a fine LOD before all its materials are visible can temporarily remove mesh parts.
Limited tile residency evicts previously visited tiles and requires reading/decoding them again.
changes: Navigation selection is centred on the camera with fixed profile-based ranges; balanced ranges are 1200/550/280m.
Expanded selection frustum and all-direction retention for models within 60m.
LOD hysteresis and coarse-outline-first triangle reservation before detail upgrades.
Fine LOD replacement requires every detail material to be visible.
Optional persistent whole-map preload loads all position tiles, available LOD bundles, and model textures, with at most two background tasks per batch and frame yields.
Preload reuses pending jobs, does not evict tiles, tracks real progress/failures, and supports cancellation and map generation invalidation.
Preferences, import/export validation, default settings, desktop settings, and Fly/Walk HUD include the stream/preload option.

limitations: Preloading means CPU-side resource residency, not uploading/drawing every highest-detail instance at once.
Frustum, screen-pixel, distance and draw budgets still defer some candidates, especially distant details.
First-use GPU upload, shader compilation and terrain detail updates can still stall briefly.
Switching back to stream stops new preload tasks and restores finite tile caching; previously loaded geometry/texture caches remain until map change or refresh.
Changing map or refreshing reconstructs in-memory resources; this is not a persistent decoded-GPU cache.
Memory requirements and performance depend on device; whole-map preload is not the default.
